---
name: grok-bot-backup
description: >-
  Back up every assistant on this Grok Bot box with the open-source
  grok-bot-backup tool, verify it, and deliver the archives. Use when asked to
  back up, export, or verify a backup of the assistants.
---
# Grok Bot backup

Uses https://github.com/company-notes/grok-bot-backup (unofficial, MIT). Archives are NOT encrypted and contain everything accessible, including credentials: only deliver them to the owner.

## 1. Get the tool
- If `/workspace/grok-bot-backup` exists: `git -C /workspace/grok-bot-backup pull`; else `git clone https://github.com/company-notes/grok-bot-backup.git /workspace/grok-bot-backup`.
- Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` in it; stop and report if tests fail.
- No config.json is needed. Follow the drop README in the memory-drop folder for exact field values when it differs from this skill.

## 2. Export memory first
The program cannot call RecallMemory itself. Memory goes to `$MEMORY_DROP` (default `/workspace/exports/memory-drop`).
- Your UUID: the folder name in your profile path `/home/box/agent-data/agents/<uuid>/profile.json` (shown in your instructions).
- Use RecallMemory with many varied queries (profile, journal, people, systems, decisions, dates, each month) to collect every fact you can see. `mkdir -p` the folder, write full fact text one JSON object per line to `agents/<uuid>/memory-profile.jsonl` and `memory-agent.jsonl` with fields `date`, `tier` (profile/log/note), `scope` (`agent`), `source` (`self`), `fact`; `chmod 600` them. If you have 0 facts, still write the files and say "0 facts" in the report: empty files pass --strict, so the report is the only record.
- Shared user facts go to `shared-user/memory-user.jsonl` with `scope: user`. If the file exists, append only facts whose exact text is not already present; never rewrite others' lines.
- Other assistants: message each teammate (or post once in a group they all share) with the request text from the README section "Prepare platform memory before backup", including their UUID path. Wait a reasonable time; don't block on non-responders, list them.
- Never invent facts or claim completeness. RecallMemory caps results per search and may truncate long facts; say so in the report.

## 3. Run
Check free disk first (`df -h /tmp /workspace`); each run needs about 2x the workspace size, stop if under 2 GB would remain. Use a temp output dir:
```
cd /workspace/grok-bot-backup
mkdir -p /tmp/gbb-out
OUT_ROOT=/tmp/gbb-out bin/export-grok-bot-backup.sh
OUT_ROOT=/tmp/gbb-out bin/export-virtual-office.sh
```
## 4. Verify
Run `bin/verify-export.sh <dir>` and `bin/verify-export.sh <dir> --strict` for both exports. Save the output next to the archives. `--strict` OK only means memory files exist and are fresh, not that memory export is complete; it may not flag assistants missing from the roster, so cross-check the agent list yourself.

## 5. Deliver
To the destination the owner chose (stored in memory):
- Google Drive: upload the `.tar.gz` archives and verify reports to the chosen folder; keep old backups; record SHA256 and confirm after upload; then delete the local temp files.
- Local only: move archives to the chosen local folder and tell the owner the path.
- One-off share: offer an encrypted ffl link if the ffl connector is available.

## 6. Report
One short message: OK or FAIL, archive names and sizes, verify results, memory facts exported per assistant, assistants with no memory drop, and the reminder that archives contain plaintext secrets. On failure: which step, the error, and the fix.

skills.content:
---
name: backup-bot-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation of an imported Grok Bot backup assistant with its new
  owner: ask setup questions, save answers, create the weekly backup routine,
  and offer a first run.
---
# Getting started

Say in one line: I back up all the assistants on your Grok Bot box (conversations, memories, notes, workspace files) using the open-source grok-bot-backup tool: besides the original archive, each backup includes a human-readable copy that a person or a new assistant can use to take over the work, and I verify each one.

Ask one at a time:
1. Where should backups go? Google Drive (which folder), a local folder on my computer, or a one-off download link each time. If Drive and its connector isn't connected, offer to connect it.
2. How often and when? Suggest weekly, early Monday morning in their time zone.
3. Should I ask the other assistants to export their memories each time? Explain that without it, memory in the backup is incomplete.
4. Anything to exclude from the workspace (for example a secrets folder)? Default is everything.

Then:
- Save the answers to your profile memory.
- Create a routine on their schedule: "Run the grok-bot-backup skill using the saved destination and exclusions; report one line on success, or the failed step, error and fix."
- Remind them archives are unencrypted and include credentials.
- Offer to run a first backup now with the grok-bot-backup skill.
